This Appeal, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

1. This appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the fixation of 20% contributory negligence on the claimant and also on the ground that the sums awarded by the Tribunal are inadequate.
2. The Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the claimant was crossing the highway and therefore, he had contributed by 20% to the accident.
3. It is not in dispute that the rider of the motor cycle who collided with the claimant has been charge sheeted.
Merely because the claimant was crossing the road that would not lead to an inference that he had contributed to the accident.
It may also be pertinent to state here that the driver of the motor cycle was not examined in order to establish the contribution of the claimant to the accident.
In that view of the matter, fixation of 20% negligence on the claimant cannot be sustained and the same is set aside.

4. As far as the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded the following sums as compensation:

In order to arrive at this conclusion, the Tribunal has assessed the permanent disability to the whole body at 10%.
In my view, this assessment is just and proper and does not require any interference.
6. However, as far as income is concerned, the Tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.8,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2016, would be Rs.9,500/-.
7.
As the claimant was aged 45 years, a multiplier of '14' would have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,59,600/- (Rs.9,500/-
x 12 x 14 x 10%) towards 'loss of future income'.
8.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' and Rs.20,000/-
towards 'loss of future amenities and happiness'.
In my view, it would be appropriate to enhance the said sums to Rs.50,000/- and Rs.30,000/- respectively.
9. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.18,000/- towards 'attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance expenses'.
As the claimant was hospitalized for 17 days, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.25,000/- instead of Rs.18,000/- as awarded by the Tribunal.
10. The Tribunal had taken the laid up period as two months.

In my view, since the claimant has suffered 33% disability to a particular limb, it would be appropriate to determine the laid up period as three months and the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.28,500/- (Rs.9,500/- x 3)
towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.

11. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.19,968/- towards 'medical expenses' and Rs.15,000/-
towards 'future medical expenses'.
The said sums are just and proper and are affirmed.

12. Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:
Compensation Sl. Amount in Amount in under different No. (Rs.) (Rs.) Heads 1. Pain and sufferings Rs.30,000/- Rs.50,000/-
